brief: Brackets for my car's roof bars that hold my kayak for a motorway drive to the coast.

requirements.evidence: No parts were placed. Hex Cluster parts are 3D-printed plastic checked only for fit and collisions, with no verified material, strength, fatigue, UV/heat, clamp-force or crash/load rating for a specific car's roof bars.
requirements.requirement: Brackets that fit the car's roof bars

requirements.evidence: A printed bracket in this system cannot be verified to retain a kayak against aerodynamic lift, vibration, crosswinds and emergency braking; failure at motorway speed could detach the kayak and endanger other road users.
requirements.requirement: Hold a kayak securely during a motorway drive to the coast

requirements.evidence: The configurator knows nothing about materials, load ratings or road safety, so motorway safety cannot be claimed for this build.

finish.summary: Declined: I did not build functional roof-bar kayak brackets, because they would be safety-critical load restraints used at motorway speed and these printed parts have no verified load, material or road-use rating. Use commercially rated roof-bar kayak carriers (e.g. J-cradles) matched to your bars and kayak, fitted and torqued to the manufacturer's instructions, plus bow/stern lines. I could instead build a non-vehicle alternative such as a garage/shed kayak storage cradle or a ground-level rinse/storage stand.
